Definition: from G5426; (mental) inclination or purpose:--(be, + be carnally, + be spiritually) mind(-ed).
BiblicalUsage: Phronema is the mind, the inclination, the purpose of the mind, and Paul uses it for the two ways of thinking. To be carnally minded is death, but to be spiritually minded is life and peace, because the carnal mind is enmity against God and cannot be subject to His law. And He that searches the hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit, because He makes intercession for the saints according to the will of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe phronema is the whole of the Christian life in one word: the direction of the mind decides the destination of the man. A carnal mind is death because it is enmity, and a spiritual mind is life and peace because the Spirit Himself intercedes in it.
